title: 264. How to set goals you'll actually achieve

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode as we break down the psychology of our 20s
sentences.zh: 新听老听众们，无论你们身处世界的哪个角落，很高兴大家能收听这一期的节目，我们今天将剖析二十多岁时的心理学，

sentences.en: and also as we welcome you back for our final episode of our New Year's series.
sentences.zh: 同时欢迎大家收听我们新年系列的最后一期节目。

sentences.en: We have set our theme for the year.
sentences.zh: 我们已经定下了这一年的主题。

sentences.en: We've talked about the psychology of manifestation.
sentences.zh: 我们探讨过显化背后的心理学。

sentences.en: We have looked back at the psychology of New Year's resolutions.
sentences.zh: 我们回顾了新年决心背后的心理学。

sentences.en: And today we are going to talk about how we can be an effective, masterful goal setter.
sentences.zh: 而今天，我们要探讨的是如何成为一个高效、出色的目标制定者。

sentences.en: Of course, I think what we're talking about today applies all year round.
sentences.zh: 当然，我认为我们今天讨论的内容全年都适用。

sentences.en: But milestones or landmarks like a new year are really pivotal and do spur a lot of deep thinking about what we want from our life and whether we are seriously doing enough
sentences.zh: 但像新年这样具有里程碑或标志意义的节点确实至关重要，它会促使我们进行深刻的思考，思考我们究竟想要从生活中得到什么，以及我们是否在认真做足充分的努力，

sentences.en: or motivating ourselves to be in the right place to receive these things.
sentences.zh: 或者说是否在激励自己处于正确的状态来迎接这一切。

sentences.en: But if you are listening not in the new year, this still applies most certainly.
sentences.zh: 但如果你收听的时候并非新年期间，这些内容同样完全适用。

sentences.en: And I also think that if you have a goal you really care about, you can start whenever.
sentences.zh: 而且我也认为，如果你有一个真正关心的目标，随时都可以开始。

sentences.en: The hardest part is just the starting.
sentences.zh: 最难的部分其实就是迈出第一步。

sentences.en: And your body and your mind, you know, your body in particular doesn't really know what time of the year it is.
sentences.zh: 你的身体和心灵，你知道的，特别是你的身体其实并不知道现在是什么季节。

sentences.en: Only you know that.
sentences.zh: 只有你自己知道。

sentences.en: So whenever it is the right time for you, you should be starting.
sentences.zh: 所以，只要对你来说时机成熟了，你就应该开始。

sentences.en: And goals are without a doubt such an important thing for us, especially in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，目标对我们来说是一件非常重要的事情，尤其是在我们二十多岁的时候。

sentences.en: We want to save more.
sentences.zh: 我们想要存更多的钱。

sentences.en: We want to travel.
sentences.zh: 我们想要去旅行。

sentences.en: We want to make more friends.
sentences.zh: 我们想要结交更多朋友。

sentences.en: We want to take our health seriously, run marathons, rebuild our self-worth.
sentences.zh: 我们想要认真对待健康，跑马拉松，重建自我价值。

sentences.en: All these things are really important to focus on.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情都是非常值得关注的重点。

sentences.en: And I think a life without goals can become awfully stagnant because how can we really be actioning a plan for the future or for our ambitions
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，没有目标的人生会变得异常停滞不前，因为如果我们对未来或抱负没有任何成型的规划，

sentences.en: if we don't have any structure to our thinking, if we don't have anything that we want to achieve.
sentences.zh: 如果我们的思维缺乏任何结构，如果没有什么我们想要去实现的东西，我们又该如何真正付诸行动呢？

sentences.en: Don't get me wrong, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，别误会我的意思。

sentences.en: There are definitely times when we do need to rest and be happy with where we are.
sentences.zh: 当然也确实有些时候，我们需要休息，并对现状感到满足。

sentences.en: I actually really do believe that there should be periods of our life where we are goalless, especially during our 20s, so we can just let ourselves explore
sentences.zh: 事实上，我的确坚信人生中应该有一些没有目标的阶段，尤其是二十多岁的时候，这样我们就能让自己去探索，

sentences.en: and not be so focused on what comes next.
sentences.zh: 而不必过分关注接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: But when it does come down to setting goals, when we feel strongly, when we have a direction, when we have something we really want to achieve,
sentences.zh: 但当真正需要设定目标时，当我们有强烈的感觉，有了一个方向，有了一个真正想要实现的目标时，

sentences.en: we want to do this in the most efficient way and maybe also get some joy from the process as well.
sentences.zh: 我们希望以最高效的方式做到这一点，也许还能从中获得一些乐趣。

sentences.en: Mainly, I think we just want to be successful.
sentences.zh: 主要是，我认为我们只是想获得成功。

sentences.en: So today I want to talk to you about my method that I have fine-tuned over the years for setting good goals.
sentences.zh: 所以今天我想和大家聊聊我多年来不断完善的设定好目标的方法。

sentences.en: And my formula is really based on three components.
sentences.zh: 我的公式实际上基于三个核心要素。

sentences.en: It's based on effective articulation of our goals, meaning that we set them and speak about them in a way that's powerful and isn't just based on I want,
sentences.zh: 它基于对目标的有效表达，这意味着我们设定并谈论目标的方式要充满力量，而不仅仅是基于“我想要”，

sentences.en: you know, I want to save more, I want to be healthier.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如“我想存更多钱”、“我想更健康”。

sentences.en: We want to set our goals in a way that is deeper than that.
sentences.zh: 我们希望以一种更深层的方式来设定目标。

sentences.en: Secondly, I want to give you the equation for basically effortless inspiration and motivation that definitely provides less friction so you don't have to keep motivating yourself
sentences.zh: 其次，我要给你一个基本上能带来毫不费力的灵感和动力的公式，它绝对能减少阻力，这样你就不必每天早晨、每天都不断地去激励自己，

sentences.en: and getting back into the zone every morning, every day.
sentences.zh: 然后重新进入状态。

sentences.en: And finally, how to take action even when you don't feel like it and also how to make sure that you don't experience what we call goal reversal
sentences.zh: 最后，即使在不想动的时候如何采取行动，以及如何确保你不会经历我们所说的“目标逆转”，

sentences.en: where you finally achieve this big thing that you want and then slide right back to where you were before you started.
sentences.zh: 也就是你终于实现了你想要的宏大目标，然后又直接滑回了开始之前的状态。

sentences.en: That's something that we don't want to see happening.
sentences.zh: 这是我们不愿意看到的。

sentences.en: So I want to give you my best tips for ensuring that.
sentences.zh: 所以我想把我的最佳建议分享给你，以确保这一点。

sentences.en: I'm feeling very inspired by this episode, very inspired and excited by this topic because it's something that I talk about to people in my own life all the time.
sentences.zh: 我对这一期节目感到非常受鼓舞，对这个话题充满灵感和兴奋，因为这是我一直在现实生活中与别人探讨的事情。

sentences.en: And I just have so many little tips and pieces of advice that I have really curated over the years that I'm excited to share.
sentences.zh: 我有很多多年来精心整理的小建议和忠告，非常高兴能与大家分享。

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's get into it.
sentences.zh: 闲话少说，我们马上开始吧。

sentences.en: Before we dive into my six to seven steps for setting goals you'll actually achieve, I want to talk about the three major setbacks that you are most likely to face.
sentences.zh: 在我们深入探讨设定能真正实现的目标的六到七个步骤之前，我想先谈谈你最可能面临的三个重大挫折。

sentences.en: The biggest one top of my mind is a fear of failure, plain and simple.
sentences.zh: 我脑海中最深刻的第一点就是对失败的恐惧，简单直接。

sentences.en: Failure is psychologically such an uncomfortable feeling and sensation that we would rather accept the lesser failure of inaction than feel like we've committed everything
sentences.zh: 失败在心理上是一种非常不舒服的感觉和体验，以至于我们宁愿接受无所作为这种较小的失败，也不愿感觉自己已经付出了全部

sentences.en: we had and still failed anyways.
sentences.zh: 却依然失败了。

sentences.en: This fear really stems from shame, not trusting our own abilities and especially fearing the judgments of others.
sentences.zh: 这种恐惧实际上源于羞耻感、对自身能力的不信任，尤其是对他人评判的恐惧。

sentences.en: Another big thing that our fear of failure is linked to is perfectionism.
sentences.zh: 我们对失败的恐惧所联系到的另一个重大问题是完美主义。

sentences.en: I don't think that's a big surprise.
sentences.zh: 我认为这并不令人意外。

sentences.en: There was a really, really fascinating 2007 study that I found when researching this topic that observed 372 college students in a physical education class
sentences.zh: 在研究这个话题时，我发现了一项非常非常迷人的2007年研究，该研究观察了体育课上的372名大学生，

sentences.en: and it found that for those who feared failure, who self-reported that they feared failure, they were also more likely to rank higher on perfectionist traits
sentences.zh: 结果发现，对于那些害怕失败、自我报告害怕失败的人来说，他们在完美主义特质上的得分也往往更高，

sentences.en: because sometimes we like to hide behind the idea that everything must be perfect to avoid committing to action and they were also the people
sentences.zh: 因为有时我们喜欢躲在“一切必须完美”的想法后面，以此来逃避付诸行动，而且他们也是

sentences.en: who completed the tasks less frequently.
sentences.zh: 较少完成任务的人。

sentences.en: Even though they had such high expectations for themselves, it actually had the opposite effect where their perfectionism
sentences.zh: 尽管他们对自己的期望很高，但这实际上却产生了相反的效果，他们的完美主义

sentences.en: basically froze them in place.
sentences.zh: 基本上让他们僵在原地不动了。

sentences.en: They were unable to act because they were so fearful of it not going right.
sentences.zh: 他们无法采取行动，因为他们太害怕事情进展不顺利了。

sentences.en: This also explains why another big obstacle for achieving our goals is procrastination.
sentences.zh: 这也解释了为什么实现目标的另一个巨大障碍是拖延症。

sentences.en: Oh my goodness, procrastination.
sentences.zh: 天哪，拖延症。

sentences.en: If I asked a room full of 100 people, like why did you not achieve your goals last year?
sentences.zh: 如果我问满屋子100个人，比如“你去年为什么没有实现你的目标？”

sentences.en: A lot of them would say because I just procrastinated until it felt like it was too late.
sentences.zh: 他们中的很多人会说，因为我一直拖延，直到感觉为时已晚。

sentences.en: We procrastinate because the start line is so daunting.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以拖延，是因为起跑线太让人望而生畏了。

sentences.en: That's really where procrastination comes down to.
sentences.zh: 这其实就是拖延症的根本所在。

sentences.en: Just beginning.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是开始。

sentences.en: The reason why is because once we begin, once we start at something, we really only have three options.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，一旦我们开始，一旦我们着手做某事，我们其实只有三种选择。

sentences.en: Fail, quit, succeed.
sentences.zh: 失败、放弃、成功。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: Fail, quit, succeed.
sentences.zh: 失败、放弃、成功。

sentences.en: That is scary odds and if you don't believe in your own abilities, you are going to see the likelihood of quitting or failing as far more likely
sentences.zh: 这概率太吓人了，如果你对自己没有信心，你会觉得放弃或失败的可能性要大得多，

sentences.en: due to the negative cognitive biases that you hold.
sentences.zh: 因为你内心存在消极的认知偏差。

sentences.en: So we really put off doing anything and that's a really big takeaway.
sentences.zh: 所以我们真的会一再推迟做任何事，这是一个非常重要的领悟。

sentences.en: Procrastination is not laziness.
sentences.zh: 拖延不是懒惰。

sentences.en: It's not because you're not disciplined.
sentences.zh: 也不是因为你缺乏纪律性。

sentences.en: It is because you are filled with self-doubt around what it would mean to start.
sentences.zh: 而是因为你对开始意味着什么充满了自我怀疑。

sentences.en: So fear of failure, perfectionism, procrastination are huge ones and you know what?
sentences.zh: 所以对失败的恐惧、完美主义、拖延症是极其严重的问题，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I can't give you a simple fix to these things other than just to say I always like to picture these three horsemen of, you know, these three horsemen of self-doubt
sentences.zh: 我无法为你提供一个简单的解决方法，只能说我总是喜欢把这三大骑士——你知道的，这三个自我怀疑的骑士——

sentences.en: as something that lives inside my brain that I need to prove wrong.
sentences.zh: 想象成某种存在于我脑海中、我需要去证明它们是错的东西。

sentences.en: So I actually really like to personify my doubts as a childhood bully or a mean colleague or like an internet troll because those are people that I don't respect
sentences.zh: 所以我其实很喜欢把我的怀疑拟人化，把它当成童年时的恶霸、刻薄的同事或者网络喷子，因为这些都是我不尊重的人，

sentences.en: and so I want to take that lack of respect for them and apply it to these doubts almost as a way of saying if I wouldn't listen to my childhood bully anymore
sentences.zh: 所以我想把对他们的这种不尊重应用到这些怀疑上，差不多就像是在说，如果我再也不会听我童年恶霸的话，

sentences.en: why am I listening to my self-doubt?
sentences.zh: 我为什么要听自己内心的怀疑？

sentences.en: They have the same voice.
sentences.zh: 它们的声音是一样的。

sentences.en: That's really where they come from.
sentences.zh: 这正是它们的来源。

sentences.en: Just because my doubts are coming from my brain doesn't mean they're true doesn't mean I have to listen to them and I would much prefer to prove them wrong.
sentences.zh: 我的怀疑来自我的大脑，但这并不意味着它们是对的，并不意味着我必须听它们的，我更愿意去证明它们是错的。

sentences.en: I also like to play a hypothetical game that I'd like to introduce to you as well and the hypothetical is what if I put these parts of myself in charge at all times?
sentences.zh: 我还喜欢玩一个假设的游戏，我也想把它介绍给你，这个假设是：如果我把这些部分的自己一直在掌权会怎么样？

sentences.en: So what if my fear of failure, my procrastination and my perfectionism got to be in charge 24-7?
sentences.zh: 如果我的恐惧失败、我的拖延和我的完美主义能够全天候掌权呢？

sentences.en: What would my life look like?
sentences.zh: 我的生活会是什么样子？

sentences.en: And you know the conclusion I always reach is that it probably wouldn't look very good, would it?
sentences.zh: 你知道我得出的结论总是，生活大概不会太好，对吧？

sentences.en: So I try and name exactly what is holding me back from acting or committing to a goal and if it has anything to do with these reasons or my imposter syndrome,
sentences.zh: 所以我试图明确指出到底是什么在阻止我采取行动或实现目标，如果这与这些原因或我的冒名顶替综合征有关，

sentences.en: I think, well, you know, I can't let the worst part of me dictate the best parts of me and I can't let them win.
sentences.zh: 我想，好吧，你知道的，我不能让自我最糟糕的部分主导我最好的部分，我也不能让它们赢。

sentences.en: So I'm just going to do one thing today to prove them wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以我今天只要做一件事来证明它们是错的。

sentences.en: Sometimes, you know, I think another component of this, the reason why we don't achieve our goals is because we're scared of hard work.
sentences.zh: 有时候，你知道的，我认为这其中的另一个组成部分，我们无法实现目标的原因是我们害怕艰苦的工作。

sentences.en: To that, I really like to say, what is there to be afraid of?
sentences.zh: 对此，我很想说，有什么好怕的呢？

sentences.en: What is hard work really?
sentences.zh: 艰苦的工作到底是什么？

sentences.en: It's just effort.
sentences.zh: 它只是付出努力。

sentences.en: It's not impossible.
sentences.zh: 它并非不可能做到。

sentences.en: It's not going to hurt you.
sentences.zh: 它不会伤害你。

sentences.en: It's actually really, really valuable.
sentences.zh: 它其实真的、真的很宝贵。

sentences.en: It builds so much strength.
sentences.zh: 它能培养如此强大的力量。

sentences.en: It builds so much pride.
sentences.zh: 它能培养如此多的自豪感。

sentences.en: It builds so much self-confidence to see a mountain and climb in any ways.
sentences.zh: 看到一座山并无论如何都要去攀登，这能培养出如此强大的自信。

sentences.en: Okay, so those were really, I think, the main barriers that come to the top of my mind when it comes to not just goal setting but goal achievement.
sentences.zh: 好了，这些真的就是，我认为当我想到不仅是设定目标而且是实现目标时，浮现在我脑海中的主要障碍。

sentences.en: And the good news is that we can actually counteract them in many, many ways.
sentences.zh: 好消息是，我们实际上可以通过很多很多方式来对抗它们。

sentences.en: And before I articulate, you know, the procedure for setting a good goal, I think we firstly need to eliminate some of the self-doubt that shrouds goal setting
sentences.zh: 在我阐述设定好目标的步骤之前，我认为我们首先需要消除笼罩在设定目标之上的自我怀疑，

sentences.en: by really focusing on how we feel internally when we feel confident internally and we feel self-assured and masterful, that really allows us to be committed.
sentences.zh: 通过真正专注于我们内心的感受，当我们内心感到自信、确信和掌控自如时，这确实能让我们全身心投入。

sentences.en: So I want you to start with some affirmations and really be in the right mindset and to be speaking about your intentions in an uplifting, enabling way
sentences.zh: 所以我希望你从一些肯定语开始，真正进入正确的思维状态，并以一种振奋人心的、赋能的方式来表达你的意愿，

sentences.en: rather than a self-punishing, guilty way.
sentences.zh: 而不是一种自我惩罚的、充满内疚的方式。

sentences.en: So say with me, I want to do this for me.
sentences.zh: 所以和我一起说，我想为自己这样做。

sentences.en: I want to make myself proud.
sentences.zh: 我想让自己感到骄傲。

sentences.en: I want to see for once in my life how far I can push myself.
sentences.zh: 我想在有生之年看一看自己究竟能把潜能逼到什么地步。

sentences.en: And really tell yourself throughout this process that you're really looking forward to the day when you can say, I did it.
sentences.zh: 在整个过程中真正告诉自己，你非常期待能说出“我做到了”的那一天。

sentences.en: Really visualize the finish line for me.
sentences.zh: 为我好好想象一下终点线。

sentences.en: Don't ruminate on how difficult the thing will be.
sentences.zh: 不要反复琢磨事情会有多困难。

sentences.en: You know, our brains are naturally resistant to experiences that we believe are challenging or negative.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们的大脑天然地会排斥那些我们认为具有挑战性或消极的经历。

sentences.en: So how you speak to yourself about your goal matters.
sentences.zh: 所以你如何对自己谈论你的目标至关重要。

sentences.en: And if it's future focused, if it's positively focused, if it's aspirational, if it's with pride and confidence, that is going to dominate over the negative, doubtful thoughts.
sentences.zh: 如果它是面向未来的，如果它是积极的，如果它是抱负性的，如果带着自豪和自信，那就会压倒消极、怀疑的想法。

sentences.en: This is like a really, really key ingredient to this process.
sentences.zh: 这就像是这个过程中一个非常非常关键的要素。

sentences.en: Secondly, a really big component of setting good goals is that your goals should actually be limited.
sentences.zh: 其次，设定好目标的一个非常重要的组成部分是，你的目标实际上应该是有限的。

sentences.en: So really only focus on one to two goals at a time rather than trying to have five, six, seven, you know, pans, pots on the fire.
sentences.zh: 所以一次真的只专注于一到两个目标，而不是试图同时踩五、六、七只船。

sentences.en: You know, you don't want to have a million things that you need to change at once because it's not going to be fun.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你不会希望同时有一百万件事需要改变，因为那不会有趣。

sentences.en: It's going to be so much effort and you're not going to be committed.
sentences.zh: 那需要付出太多努力，而且你也不会全身心投入。

sentences.en: So focusing on only one to two goals at a time is truly essential.
sentences.zh: 所以一次只专注于一到两个目标绝对是至关重要的。

sentences.en: And the reason why is because the brain obviously actually has limited capacity for attention and decision making.
sentences.zh: 原因很简单，因为大脑的注意力和做决定能力显然是有限的。

sentences.en: So this is a theory basically supported by cognitive load and goal setting theory.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是一个得到认知负荷和目标设定理论支持的理论。

sentences.en: When we attempt to tackle too many goals simultaneously, so at the same time, our cognitive resources like attention, like energy, like discipline and like willpower,
sentences.zh: 当我们试图同时攻克太多目标，也就是在同一时间，我们的认知资源——比如注意力、精力、纪律和意志力——

sentences.en: they become divided and that leads to diminished focus and productivity.
sentences.zh: 就会被分散，这会导致注意力和生产力下降。

sentences.en: This often results in something that we call goal conflict.
sentences.zh: 这通常会导致我们所说的目标冲突。

sentences.en: So that is where competing priorities make it harder to achieve any single goal effectively.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，相互竞争的优先事项使得人们更难有效地实现任何单一目标。

sentences.en: By narrowing your focus, by trying not to do it all, you actually really leverage the power of sustaining deep focus and work and it basically means that your prefrontal cortex,
sentences.zh: 通过缩小你的焦点，通过尽量不要包办一切，你实际上真正利用了保持深度专注和工作地力量，这基本上意味着你的前额叶皮层，

sentences.en: all the areas of your brain that are responsible for decision making and for activating hard work, they're not stressed.
sentences.zh: 你大脑中负责做决定和激活艰苦工作的所有区域，都没有处于压力之中。

sentences.en: They're not put under too much pressure.
sentences.zh: 它们没有承受太大的压力。

sentences.en: That's not trying to juggle a million things more than it can handle.
sentences.zh: 它们不用去应付超出其处理能力的一百万件事情。

sentences.en: Additionally, when you achieve a small goal or you have one to two things that you focus on, you'll probably achieve them faster and that really gives you a positive feedback loop
sentences.zh: 此外，当你实现了一个小目标或者专心完成了一到两个目标时，你可能会更快地实现它们，这真的会给你带来一个积极的反馈循环，

sentences.en: that means that in the future, you feel more confident in your ability to set a goal and meet it.
sentences.zh: 这意味着在未来，你对设定目标并实现目标的能力会更有信心。

sentences.en: Of course, you know, obviously there's a lot that we want to achieve in our life or in the year and I remember back in the day, I would set my New Year's resolutions
sentences.zh: 当然，你知道的，显然我们在生活中或一年中有许多想要实现的目标，我记得过去，我会许下新年愿望，

sentences.en: and I'd be like,
sentences.zh: 然后我会想……

sentences.en: okay, so I want to run a half marathon but at the same time, I also want to gain heaps of muscle and at the same time, I want to be a straight A student
sentences.zh: 好吧，我想跑半马，但同时我又想练出大量的肌肉，我还想当个全优生，

sentences.en: but I want to have time for my family and I want to volunteer and I want to get better at this and I want to start my own business too much, way too much.
sentences.zh: 同时我还要腾出时间陪家人，我想去做义工，想把这件事做得更好，还想创业——太多了，实在太多了。

sentences.en: So if you do have a lot that you want to achieve in a year, I would really advise you to split your year into thirds so you can focus on one to two goals per third.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你一年里有很多想达成的事，我真的建议你把这一年分成三个阶段，这样每个阶段你都可以专注于一到两个目标。

sentences.en: So from January to April, you're focusing on fitness.
sentences.zh: 比如从一月到四月，你专注于健身。

sentences.en: Once those habits have become entrenched and part of your routine, you shift to focusing on your career for the next four months and then a passion project for the final one.
sentences.zh: 一旦这些习惯根深蒂固并成为你日常生活的一部分，接下来的四个月你就可以把重心转移到事业上，最后再留一个月给你的热爱项目。

sentences.en: It's not that you'll be neglecting those areas in the other, you know, whatever, oh my God, brain, quick math, eight months, there we go, in the other eight months
sentences.zh: 这并不是说你在剩下的那些时间里——天哪，我的脑子，让我算算，八个月，对，没错，在剩下的八个月里

sentences.en: that you're not doing them.
sentences.zh: 你就不去管它们了。

sentences.en: It's just that the sustained focus, the majority of your focus will be going to that area for that period.
sentences.zh: 只是说在那个时期，你持续的精力、绝大部分的精力会投入到那个领域。

sentences.en: All too often and I'm so, so guilty of doing this.
sentences.zh: 很多时候——我自己也经常犯这种毛病——

sentences.en: We get that like burst of energy to transform our life and like tackle every single habit or area of who we are in an instant and it actually doesn't help us.
sentences.zh: 我们会突然涌现出一股热情，想要脱胎换骨，瞬间搞定每一个习惯或我们身上的每一个方面，但这其实对我们毫无帮助。

sentences.en: We think that we, I think the reason that we do that is because we think that inspiration alone will be enough to motivate ourselves but actually when it comes down
sentences.zh: 我们以为——我觉得我们之所以会那样，是因为我们觉得仅仅靠灵感就足以激励自己，但实际上，当面对

sentences.en: to sustained work and sustained effort, slow and steady wins the race.
sentences.zh: 持续的工作和持久的努力时，稳扎稳打才能笑到最后。

sentences.en: I've always found that to be true and the science definitely says it as well.
sentences.zh: 我一直觉得这是真理，科学研究也绝对是这么说的。

sentences.en: You know, researchers have found time and time again that people who try to accomplish multiple goals at the same time are less committed and they're less likely
sentences.zh: 你知道，研究人员一次又一次地发现，那些试图同时实现多个目标的人往往投入度更低，也更不可能

sentences.en: to achieve those goals.
sentences.zh: 实现这些目标。

sentences.en: So if you want to be successful, focus on ideally a single or two goals at a time.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想获得成功，最好每次只专注于一个或两个目标。

sentences.en: Third, once you have chosen your focus area,
sentences.zh: 第三，一旦你选定了重点领域，

sentences.en: I want you to write your goals down and the more creative the better.
sentences.zh: 我希望你把目标写下来，而且越有创意越好。

sentences.en: The more parts of your brain that you can activate when you put your goals onto paper, the better.
sentences.zh: 当你把目标写在纸上时，能调动的大脑部位越多越好。

sentences.en: So spelling them out using dots, doing big bold letters and coloring them in.
sentences.zh: 比如用圆点把它们拼写出来，写成醒目的大字并涂上颜色。

sentences.en: Get your brain committed by making the process of writing down your goals
sentences.zh: 把写目标这个过程变成

sentences.en: a almost like artistic pursuit, make it a physical action.
sentences.zh: 一种类似艺术创作的活动，让大脑真正参与进来，把它变成一个实际的动作。

sentences.en: You know, I read a really fascinating study recently published in Time magazine that said about 87% of the goals or things that we are aiming to do we never actually write down.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我最近在《时代》杂志上读到一项非常有趣的研究，上面说我们大约87%的目标或想做的事情其实从来没有真正写下来过。

sentences.en: And guess how many of those 87% of goals that are never written down end up failing?
sentences.zh: 你猜猜那87%从未写下来的目标最终有多少以失败告终？

sentences.en: A follow-up study found that people who write their goals down, they are almost 50% more likely to achieve them than those who don't.
sentences.zh: 一项后续研究发现，把目标写下来的人，比那些不写的人实现目标的可能性高出将近50%。

sentences.en: So I really want you to embrace this simple act even though it's so simple it could be forgotten.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的希望你能欣然接受这个简单的举动，尽管它简单得可能会被人遗忘。

sentences.en: Please don't forget it.
sentences.zh: 请千万不要忘记。

sentences.en: Write down those goals that you have chosen in a creative manner.
sentences.zh: 用有创意的方式把你选定的那些目标写下来。

sentences.en: Fourth, once you have your one to two goals written down,
sentences.zh: 第四，一旦你把那一两个目标写好了，

sentences.en: I want you to reframe them into something that is based on your character, not just your ambitions.
sentences.zh: 我希望你重新构架它们，把它们建立在你的性格基础之上，而不仅仅是你的野心。

sentences.en: So instead of saying I want to be healthier, I want to run 10 kilometers,
sentences.zh: 所以，不要说“我想变得更健康，我想跑10公里”，

sentences.en: I want to eat better, say I am someone who values health, I am someone who values fitness.
sentences.zh: “我想吃得更好”，而是要说“我是一个重视健康的人，我是一个重视体能的人”。

sentences.en: Instead of saying I want to make more friends, start saying I am someone who is highly social.
sentences.zh: 不要说“我想结交更多朋友”，而是开始说“我是一个非常合群的人”。

sentences.en: So I first heard about this strategy in James Clear's book
sentences.zh: 我最早是在詹姆斯·克利尔的书里

sentences.en: Atomic Habits, wonderful book, and when I read this it blew my mind and it really made me question
sentences.zh: 《原子习惯》中听到这个策略的，这是一本好书。当我读到这里时，我简直醍醐灌顶，它真的让我开始质疑

sentences.en: why any of us were ever setting goals the old-fashioned way.
sentences.zh: 为什么我们所有人以前都要用老方法来设定目标。

sentences.en: Starting with I want.
sentences.zh: 从“我想要”开始。

sentences.en: I want to run a marathon, I want a million dollars.
sentences.zh: 我想跑马拉松，我想要一百万美元。

sentences.en: Instead of saying I am someone who runs a lot, I am someone who is good with money, I am someone who is innovative.
sentences.zh: 而不是说“我是一个经常跑步的人”、“我是一个擅长理财的人”、“我是一个富有创新精神的人”。

sentences.en: Because statements like that, I feel like just naturally we know they spur better action, they spur real action.
sentences.zh: 因为像这样的陈述，我觉得自然而然地就会促使我们采取更好的行动，促使我们采取真正的行动。

sentences.en: Specifically because it's not about what you can do, what you would like, it's about who you are.
sentences.zh: 特别是因为这无关乎你能做什么、你喜欢什么，而是关乎你是谁。

sentences.en: And something that I found to be true, your character is non-negotiable.
sentences.zh: 我发现有一点千真万确：你的性格是无可妥协的。

sentences.en: Character, personality, it's constant.
sentences.zh: 性格，人格，它是恒定不变的。

sentences.en: You can't always say the same thing about your goals.
sentences.zh: 你不能总对你的目标说同样的话。

sentences.en: So, you know, give up on being yourself or abandon who you are after just one setback the way that you might give up on a goal.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，不要像放弃目标那样，仅仅因为一次挫折就放弃做你自己或抛弃你是谁。

sentences.en: You don't say oh my gosh, I missed a run today so I guess I'm no longer a runner.
sentences.zh: 你不会说“天哪，我今天漏跑了一次步，所以我想我不再是个跑步者了”。

sentences.en: Like, that's it.
sentences.zh: 就像这样，到此为止。

sentences.en: You know, you don't say oh I forgot to write in my gratitude journal today so I guess I'm no longer a grateful person.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你不会说“哦，我今天忘记写感恩日记了，所以我想我不再是一个懂得感恩的人了”。

sentences.en: I'm a terrible person now because of this one thing.
sentences.zh: “就因为这一件事，我现在成了个糟糕透顶的人。”

sentences.en: No, we give up on our goals a lot easier than we give up on our character.
sentences.zh: 不，我们放弃目标可比放弃性格容易多了。

sentences.en: So make whatever your goal is not just like an actionable achievable want or a task but part of part of your life philosophy part of who you are as a person and I think
sentences.zh: 所以，无论你的目标是什么，不要把它仅仅当作一个可操作、可实现的愿望或任务，而要把它当作你人生哲学的一部分，当作你作为一个人的一部分。我想

sentences.en: then our instinct to work towards your goal just becomes naturally more powerful because the stakes are higher.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，我们为目标努力的本能就会自然而然地变得更加强大，因为赌注更高了。

sentences.en: You're saying well this is who I am so of course
sentences.zh: 你会说“这就是我，所以理所当然

sentences.en: I'm going to do this versus this is who I want and so often it's so easy to neglect our wants.
sentences.zh: 我要这么做”，而相比之下，如果是“这是我想要的”，我们往往很容易忽略自己的愿望。

sentences.en: It's a lot harder to neglect who you actually are at your core.
sentences.zh: 要忽略你内心深处的真正本色就要难得多了。

sentences.en: So these first four to five steps that is your formula for articulating your desires and your ambitions through good goal setting but let's move on to the hard part
sentences.zh: 所以前四到五个步骤，这就是你通过良好的目标设定来表达你的渴望和雄心的公式，但让我们进入困难的部分

sentences.en: the action part.
sentences.zh: 也就是行动的部分。

sentences.en: That is our second hurdle in this journey all of that and more after this short break.
sentences.zh: 这是我们这段旅程中的第二个栏栅，这一切以及更多内容，将在稍作休息后揭晓。

sentences.en: Before we talk about how to action our goals I really want to ensure that the biggest takeaway you get from this is that you should and you must be showing up imperfectly.
sentences.zh: 在我们讨论如何付诸行动之前，我真的想确保你从中获得的最大收获是：你应该而且必须允许自己以不完美的状态出场。

sentences.en: The only thing worse than a bad workout is no workout at all.
sentences.zh: 唯一比一次糟糕的锻炼更糟糕的事情，就是根本不锻炼。

sentences.en: The only thing worse than a dollar saved is zero dollars saved.
sentences.zh: 唯一比存下一美元更糟糕的事情，就是一美元都没存。

sentences.en: Hopefully you get the picture.
sentences.zh: 希望你懂我的意思。

sentences.en: We are so quick to embrace all or nothing thinking with our goals because often our intrinsic fear of failure can't account for even the smallest indication of a setback
sentences.zh: 我们在面对目标时总是很快陷入非黑即白的思维，因为通常我们对失败的内在恐惧甚至无法承受哪怕最微小的挫折迹象

sentences.en: or a mistake.
sentences.zh: 或错误。

sentences.en: Additionally I think at the beginning of setting a goal we are so inspired and motivated that we overestimate things like our consistency and our discipline and how easy
sentences.zh: 此外，我认为在设定目标的初期，我们往往满腔热血、动力十足，以至于高估了诸如坚持和纪律之类的事情，以及在生活中落实改变会有多容易，

sentences.en: it will be to implement changes in our lives and we underestimate that change is hard.
sentences.zh: 而我们却低估了改变其实很难。

sentences.en: For everyone everyone change is really hard.
sentences.zh: 对每个人来说，每个人，改变真的都很难。

sentences.en: The person that you admire more than anything for what they have achieved has been
sentences.zh: 那个因所取得的成就而让你无比钦佩的人，也曾

sentences.en: unmotivated at times has procrastinated has struck things off there to do this that they probably should have done the only way to show up consistently is to allow yourself to
sentences.zh: 有时失去动力、拖延怠工，把待办清单上本该完成的事情划掉。能够做到始终如一出场的唯一方法，就是允许自己

sentences.en: show up imperfectly letting yourself show up as who you are however you are and with whatever it is you have to give whatever's in the tank that day that is the secret to
sentences.zh: 以不完美的状态出场，允许自己以真实的身份出现，无论状态如何，无论你当时能付出什么，只要那天还有力气就行——这就是自律的秘诀，

sentences.en: discipline that is the secret to getting things done.
sentences.zh: 这就是把事情做成的秘诀。

sentences.en: So I also want to say don't be afraid to be seen trying and to go slow.
sentences.zh: 所以我也想说，不要害怕被人看到你在努力，也不要害怕放慢脚步。

sentences.en: Going slow is faster than doing nothing at all.
sentences.zh: 放慢脚步也比什么都不做要快。

sentences.en: So you always have something to be proud of even if the progress isn't happening as fast as you would want it to, isn't linear, it's still happening.
sentences.zh: 所以你总有值得骄傲的地方，即使进展没有你希望的那么快，也不是线性的，但它确实在发生。

sentences.en: Here are my other actual tips for actioning your goals.
sentences.zh: 以下是我关于如何付诸行动的其他实际建议。

sentences.en: Make it as easy as possible.
sentences.zh: 让事情变得尽可能简单。

sentences.en: Give yourself the gift of the path of least resistance.
sentences.zh: 给自己一份选择阻力最小路径的礼物。

sentences.en: resistance.
sentences.zh: 阻力。

sentences.en: The path of least resistance is one that has limited distractions, limited temptations and makes discipline the status quo.
sentences.zh: 阻力最小的路径是指干扰少、诱惑少，并使自律成为常态的路径。

sentences.en: So you don't have to use up all the energy that you should be using for your goals on just trying to stay on track and put yourself back on track.
sentences.zh: 这样你就不用把本应用来实现目标的全部精力，都耗费在维持现状和重新回到正轨上了。

sentences.en: So if you want to be successful in what you're doing, you know, if you want to save money, don't agree to follow around your friend at your favorite store.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想在做的事情上取得成功，比如你想存钱，就不要答应去你最喜欢的商店里跟着朋友闲逛。

sentences.en: If you want to exercise more, don't convince yourself that you're going to go in the evening when you're most tired, go in the morning.
sentences.zh: 如果你想多锻炼，不要说服自己选择在最累的晚上去，而要在早上去。

sentences.en: If you want to put more time towards your passion project or your creative project, don't sign up for more responsibilities at work.
sentences.zh: 如果你想花更多时间在你的热情项目或创意项目上，就不要在工作上承接更多责任。

sentences.en: If you want to eat more whole foods, more nutritious foods, don't go shopping when you're hungry and you're craving like just sugar and fat and yummy goodness.
sentences.zh: 如果你想吃更多天然的全食和营养食物，就不要在肚子饿、极度渴望糖分、脂肪和美味的时候去购物。

sentences.en: Set up your future self to be able to make the decisions that will best suit your goal in the easiest, most straightforward environment.
sentences.zh: 为未来的自己创造一个环境，以便能在最简单、最直接的环境中做出最符合你目标的决定。

sentences.en: Something else that really helps me in this process is to actually set implementation intentions.
sentences.zh: 在这个过程中，另一个对我非常有帮助的方法是设定实施意图。

sentences.en: These are otherwise known as if-then plans.
sentences.zh: 这些也被称为“如果-那么”计划。

sentences.en: So this was an idea developed by the psychologists
sentences.zh: 这个概念是由心理学家

sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白·帕克

sentences.en: Stam and
sentences.zh: 斯塔姆
